briefdescription.para: Construct with a buffer that is owned by the caller.

detaileddescription.para: This constructor allows us to use data that is owned by the caller. The data must stay around as long as this object is valid.

memberdef.argsstring: (ArrayRef< uint8_t > Data, bool IsLittleEndian, uint8_t AddressSize)
memberdef.name: DataExtractor

briefdescription.para: Get the data pointed to by this extractor.
Get the endianness for this extractor.
Get the address size for this extractor.
Set the address size for this extractor.
Extract a C string from *offset_ptr.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a pointer to a C String from the data at the offset pointed to by offset_ptr. A variable length NULL terminated C string will be extracted and the offset_ptr will be updated with the offset of the byte that follows the NULL terminator byte.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.

A pointer to an Error object. Upon return the Error object is set to indicate the result (success/failure) of the function. If the Error object is already set when calling this function, no extraction is performed.

simplesect.para: A pointer to the C string value in the data. If the offset pointed to by offset_ptr is out of bounds, or if the offset plus the length of the C string is out of bounds, NULL will be returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract a C string from the location given by the cursor.

detaileddescription.para: In case of an extraction error, or if the cursor is already in an error state, a nullptr is returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract a C string from *offset_ptr.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a StringRef for the C String from the data at the offset pointed to by offset_ptr. A variable length NULL terminated C string will be extracted and the offset_ptr will be updated with the offset of the byte that follows the NULL terminator byte.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.

A pointer to an Error object. Upon return the Error object is set to indicate the result (success/failure) of the function. If the Error object is already set when calling this function, no extraction is performed.

simplesect.para: A StringRef for the C string value in the data. If the offset pointed to by offset_ptr is out of bounds, or if the offset plus the length of the C string is out of bounds, a default-initialized StringRef will be returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract a C string (as a StringRef) from the location given by the cursor.

detaileddescription.para: In case of an extraction error, or if the cursor is already in an error state, a default-initialized StringRef is returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract a fixed length string from *OffsetPtr and consume Length bytes.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a StringRef for the string from the data at the offset pointed to by OffsetPtr. A fixed length C string will be extracted and the OffsetPtr will be advanced by Length bytes.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.
The length of the fixed length string to extract. If there are not enough bytes in the data to extract the full string, the offset will be left unmodified.

A set of characters to trim from the end of the string. Fixed length strings are commonly either NULL terminated by one or more zero bytes. Some clients have one or more spaces at the end of the string, but a good default is to trim the NULL characters.

simplesect.para: A StringRef for the C string value in the data. If the offset pointed to by OffsetPtr is out of bounds, or if the offset plus the length of the C string is out of bounds, a default-initialized StringRef will be returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract a fixed number of bytes from the specified offset.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a StringRef for the bytes from the data at the offset pointed to by OffsetPtr. A fixed length C string will be extracted and the OffsetPtr will be advanced by Length bytes.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.
The number of bytes to extract. If there are not enough bytes in the data to extract all of the bytes, the offset will be left unmodified.

A pointer to an Error object. Upon return the Error object is set to indicate the result (success/failure) of the function. If the Error object is already set when calling this function, no extraction is performed.

simplesect.para: A StringRef for the extracted bytes. If the offset pointed to by OffsetPtr is out of bounds, or if the offset plus the length is out of bounds, a default-initialized StringRef will be returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract a fixed number of bytes from the location given by the cursor.

detaileddescription.para: In case of an extraction error, or if the cursor is already in an error state, a default-initialized StringRef is returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract an unsigned integer of size byte_size from *offset_ptr.

detaileddescription.para: Extract a single unsigned integer value and update the offset pointed to by offset_ptr. The size of the extracted integer is specified by the byte_size argument. byte_size should have a value greater than or equal to one and less than or equal to eight since the return value is 64 bits wide. Any byte_size values less than 1 or greater than 8 will result in nothing being extracted, and zero being returned.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.
The size in byte of the integer to extract.

A pointer to an Error object. Upon return the Error object is set to indicate the result (success/failure) of the function. If the Error object is already set when calling this function, no extraction is performed.

simplesect.para: The unsigned integer value that was extracted, or zero on failure.

briefdescription.para: Extract an unsigned integer of the given size from the location given by the cursor.

detaileddescription.para: In case of an extraction error, or if the cursor is already in an error state, zero is returned.

briefdescription.para: Extract an signed integer of size byte_size from *offset_ptr.

detaileddescription.para: Extract a single signed integer value (sign extending if required) and update the offset pointed to by offset_ptr. The size of the extracted integer is specified by the byte_size argument. byte_size should have a value greater than or equal to one and less than or equal to eight since the return value is 64 bits wide. Any byte_size values less than 1 or greater than 8 will result in nothing being extracted, and zero being returned.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.
The size in bytes of the integer to extract.

simplesect.para: The sign extended signed integer value that was extracted, or zero on failure.

briefdescription.para: Extract an pointer from *offset_ptr.

detaileddescription.para: Extract a single pointer from the data and update the offset pointed to by offset_ptr. The size of the extracted pointer is getAddressSize(), so the address size has to be set correctly prior to extracting any pointer values.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.

simplesect.para: The extracted pointer value as a 64 integer.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.

briefdescription.para: Extract count uint8_t values from *offset_ptr.

detaileddescription.para: Extract count uint8_t values from the binary data at the offset pointed to by offset_ptr, and advance the offset on success. The extracted values are copied into dst.

parameterdescription.para: A pointer to an offset within the data that will be advanced by the appropriate number of bytes if the value is extracted correctly. If the offset is out of bounds or there are not enough bytes to extract this value, the offset will be left unmodified.
A buffer to copy count uint8_t values into. dst must be large enough to hold all requested data.
The number of uint8_t values to extract.

simplesect.para: dst if all values were properly extracted and copied, NULL otherise.

briefdescription.para: Extract Count uint8_t values from the location given by the cursor and store them into the destination buffer.

detaileddescription.para: In case of an extraction error, or if the cursor is already in an error state, a nullptr is returned and the destination buffer is left unchanged.

briefdescription.para: Extract Count uint8_t values from the location given by the cursor and store them into the destination vector.

detaileddescription.para: The vector is resized to fit the extracted data. In case of an extraction error, or if the cursor is already in an error state, the destination vector is left unchanged and cursor is placed into an error state.

detaileddescription.para: No-op if the cursor is in an error state.

briefdescription.para: Return true iff the cursor is at the end of the buffer, regardless of the error state of the cursor.

detaileddescription.para: The only way both eof and error states can be true is if one attempts a read while the cursor is at the very end of the data buffer.

briefdescription.para: Test the validity of offset.

simplesect.para: true if offset is a valid offset into the data in this object, false otherwise.

briefdescription.para: Test the availability of length bytes of data from offset.

simplesect.para: true if offset is a valid offset and there are length bytes available at that offset, false otherwise.

briefdescription.para: Test the availability of enough bytes of data for a pointer from offset.

detaileddescription.para: The size of a pointer is getAddressSize().

simplesect.para: true if offset is a valid offset and there are enough bytes for a pointer available at that offset, false otherwise.

briefdescription.para: Return the number of bytes in the underlying buffer.
If it is possible to read Size bytes at offset Offset, returns true.

detaileddescription.para: Otherwise, returns false. If E is not nullptr, also sets the error object to indicate an error.
